structuredOutput.stance: Ship a simple web app first; desktop cost and packaging exceed what a two-person v1 needs.

recommendation.why: One codebase, no installers, and instant updates fit a small budget. Freelancers can open it in a browser on any machine. Desktop OS work can wait until the workflow is proven.

options.name: Simple web app
options.for: Fastest to ship, cheap hosting, easy sharing and updates for two builders.
options.against: Weaker offline use and less native OS integration than a desktop app.

options.name: Desktop app
options.for: Offline work, local files, and a more native feel for daily use.
options.against: Installers, updates, and multi-OS support raise cost and delay the first version.

options.name: Web now, desktop later
options.for: Validates the product cheaply, then wraps only features that need the desktop.
options.against: A later port still costs time if the web data model is poorly designed.

options.name: Cross-platform shell
options.for: One UI can later run as web and desktop with shared logic.
options.against: Framework and packaging overhead is heavy for an unproven first version.

claims.text: A two-person team ships a browser MVP faster than multi-OS desktop installers.
A task tool's first value is capture, lists, and reminders, not deep OS access.
Web updates reach every user without an app-store or installer cycle.

risks: Offline-heavy freelancers may reject a web-only tool.
Browser limits can block local-file workflows you later need.
A thin web MVP can look unfinished next to polished desktop competitors.
unknowns: Do users need local files or only cloud tasks?
Which devices do freelancers actually use daily?
structuredOutput.would_change_my_mind: Strong proof that offline local files are required on day one.
